\section{Results}
\label{sec:results}

\subsection{Main comparison}
Table~\ref{tab:main-results} reports accuracy, inference cost, and paired McNemar exact-test $p$-values relative to direct generation. On Llama~3.1~8B, search achieves an accuracy of $0.159 \pm 0.012$, below direct generation ($0.223$), structured prompting ($0.262$), and Best-of-$N$ ($0.236 \pm 0.012$). Search uses an average of 13.4 calls and 13,722 tokens per question, compared with 14 calls and 22,959 tokens for Best-of-$N$. On Llama~3.1~70B, search reaches $0.362 \pm 0.015$, compared with $0.377$ for direct generation. The reported McNemar tests do not show a statistically significant difference from direct generation at the $0.05$ level.

\subsection{Search ablations}
Table~\ref{tab:ablations} presents the ablation results across three seeds. The fixed-scoring variant achieves the highest accuracy among the tested ablations ($0.190 \pm 0.012$), compared with $0.159 \pm 0.012$ for the frozen-search reference. The random, steps, and vote scoring variants achieve accuracies of $0.133 \pm 0.031$, $0.136 \pm 0.016$, and $0.108 \pm 0.008$, respectively. Increasing the branching factor to five yields $0.115 \pm 0.020$. Increasing the search budget to 28 calls does not improve accuracy over the reference, reaching $0.154 \pm 0.020$ with 23.9 calls per question. Removing state prediction yields $0.159 \pm 0.029$ while reducing the mean call count to 3.9 per question.

\subsection{Candidate coverage and error patterns}
For 8B search, a correct candidate is proposed at the root for approximately 31\% of questions, while final accuracy is approximately 16\%. For 70B search, root candidate coverage is approximately 59\%, compared with final accuracy of approximately 36\%. The score-separation AUC is approximately 0.58 for 8B and 0.53 for 70B. These metrics describe the relationship between candidate generation, scoring, and the final selected answer.

Across search runs, the mean error counts per run differ by error category. The 8B runs average 4.00 format errors, 75.67 inapplicable-action errors, and 29.67 not-closer errors; the corresponding 70B averages are 0.33, 45.00, and 37.67, respectively. Accuracy also varies by domain; the per-domain results are reported in the analysis output.

\subsection{Token-budget robustness}
We compare search with Best-of-$N$ under a shared cap of 14,000 tokens per question, using $N=8$ for Best-of-$N$. Across three seeds, search achieves an accuracy of $0.151 \pm 0.018$, while Best-of-$N$ achieves $0.228 \pm 0.022$. Search averages 12.16 calls and 11,230 tokens per question; Best-of-$N$ averages 7.72 calls and 12,348 tokens. Although both methods share the same token cap, their actual token consumption differs.
